synthesis.body: A socket timeout applies per `recv`, not per `read()`. So `fp.read(cap + 1)` against a server that sends one byte at a time resets the clock on every byte, and the read is bounded only by cap x timeout — 64 KiB at 5 s is hours. Any deadline you enforce *before* the request does not constrain the body read at all. Read in chunks and re-check the deadline between them. Matters most on a credential or auth path, where the fetch target can be attacker-influenced (e.g. a URL taken from a WWW-Authenticate header) and the caller is a synchronous operator command that simply hangs.

title: One large socket read is unbounded in wall-clock even with a socket timeout
